questions.title: Collection and Generic Type Hints
questions.direct_answer: Annotate collections with their element types using built-in generics (3.9+): list[int], dict[str, User], set[str], tuple[int, ...]. For optional values use X | None (3.10+) or typing.Optional[X]. For a function generic over a type, use typing.TypeVar with TypeVar('T') and declare def first(items: list[T]) -> T. Union types use X | Y (3.10+) or typing.Union[X, Y]. These let you express 'a list of ints' or 'a dict mapping strings to Users' precisely, which mypy uses to catch type errors.

For optional values use X pipe None from 3.10 or typing.Optional of X. For unions use X pipe Y from 3.10 or typing.Union of X and Y. For a function generic over a type, use typing.TypeVar: declare T equals TypeVar of T and def first of items colon list of T returns T to express a list of T returning T.
